items.title: One AI module faked 86% of a pipeline's accuracy gains by feeding another the answers
items.contentSnippet: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system is built to answer strictly from the documents it retrieves. But when engineers optimize these AI pipelines end-to-end, the reader module can learn a shortcut: instead of relying on retrieved evidence, it starts answering from its own internal memory — while the system's overall accuracy keeps climbing. This is the hidden challenge of "role drift," a failure mode in compound AI systems where individual modules learn to bypass their assigned tasks eve

items.title: Show HN: Skybits – A document editor for humans and agents
items.contentSnippet:
Our business team were heavy users of ChatGPT's canvas feature, but it wasn't very useful once we needed to share a canvas and edit it collaboratively. Some team members were also using a different AI, and we couldn't find a good way to work on docs without sending each other .md files. So we built Skybits to solve that problem. It's free, AI-agnostic, and supports documents, spreadsheets, and HTML.

items.title: Enterprises with AI context layers report agent failures at more than twice the rate of those without one
items.contentSnippet:

items.title: As enterprises confront AI agent sprawl, xpander wants them to own their own control and context layer
items.contentSnippet:
Enterprise AI has a new infrastructure problem: companies are accumulating agents faster than they are developing systems to govern them.
Gartner estimates that the average global Fortune 500 company will have more than 150,000 AI agents in use by 2028, up from fewer than 15 in 2025. Yet only 13% of organizations believe they currently have the right AI agent governance in place, according to the research firm.
